messages:
rachel: Heads-up from QA: after yesterday's routing-policy console rollout, a few customers reported sudden quota burn spikes and some SDKs throwing errors when route hints contain commas. can we triage?

kevin: saw the alert. dashboard: https://console.redwood.dev/d/routing?panelId=7  spikes start ~03:40 UTC. token-meter shows bump, but traces show repeated retries from clients that then hit quota faster.

zoe: quick root cause guess: console started returning route hints as a comma-separated list in X-Route-Hints instead of JSON array to be compact. older SDK parsers (py & go) split on comma and treat each element as a separate route -> double-counting in token attribution middleware.

harry: additionally, TS SDK had strict schema validation in v4.2.0 that rejects commas inside a single token; throws ValidationError which upstream treats as 4xx and triggers retry logic.

rachel: that explains both retry storms and quota mis-attribution. ops: can we temporarily revert the routing-policy payload change?

deploy-bot: Rollback requested for feature flag "routing-policy-compact-hints". Initiating rollback for 100% rollout -> original shape. ETA ~5m.

ci-bot: Created issues: SDK-600 (py/go: tolerant route-hint parsing + idempotent token attribution), SDK-601 (ts: relax schema to allow comma-containing hints). Links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/600, https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/601

kevin: ops: adding a temporary dashboard filter to show retry count per org and gating any org with >10 retries/min to a debug-queue to prevent quota burn.

zoe: patch plan: 1) console: revert payload shape (done by rollback) 2) sdk: implement tolerant parse that accepts comma-separated or JSON array and normalizes to a canonical list without double-counting, 3) add unit tests + e2e on quota ledger. I'll open PRs for py/go.

harry: I'll update TS SDK with schema merge that accepts both shapes for one release cycle and logs a deprecation warning. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/1102

rachel: timeline: can we get SDK patches out within 6 hours so we can re-rollout the compact format with negotiation header? product wants compact token eventually but not at cost of quota surprises.

ci-bot: PR created for py SDK: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-py/pull/912 "tolerant route-hint parsing + idempotent attribution". CI queued.

kevin: ops note: added an alert "client-retry-spike" (threshold 5x baseline for 5m) and a dashboard widget showing header shapes frequency (raw) so we can detect unexpected formats pre-rollout.

zoe: also adding a migration test in the console CI that runs a matrix of SDK versions against new header shapes to catch compatibility issues before deploy. filing ticket CONSOLE-802.

rachel: one more ask: telemetry team please add a tag to quota samples that indicates whether route-hints were normalized by SDK or passed-through. will help us reconcile ledger differences.

ci-bot: Telemetry ticket created: TELEMETRY-443.

harry: TS patch merged and published to npm as v4.2.1 with tolerant schema and warning logs.

zoe: py/go PRs green, releasing py v1.3.5 and go v0.9.7 with fixes. changelogs include: "Treat X-Route-Hints as optional; accept JSON array or comma-separated list; do not double-count tokens; upgrade recommended."

kevin: ops: re-enable canary for routing-policy-compact-hints to 5% but behind negotiation: server will only send compact hints if client includes Accept-Route-Hints=1 in handshake.

rachel: good. product: we'll monitor for 24h with rollback gates: any org seeing >2x quota delta vs baseline or client retry spike -> immediate rollback. thank you team for fast coordination.

zoe: follow-ups: SDK-600/601 for permanent fixes, CONSOLE-802 for CI compatibility matrix, TELEMETRY-443 for tagging. leaving thread for monitoring updates. :thumbsup:
